package_info.package_manager: Linux distribution package manager (e.g., apt, yum, pacman)
package_info.why_malicious: The xz-utils package (specifically xz/liblzma) was backdoored to enable remote, unauthorized access and code execution on affected systems. The malicious code was introduced via a sophisticated supply chain attack, compromising the integrity of a widely used open-source compression library.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when sshd is started or used)
execution_context.file_location: liblzma code within xz-utils (liblzma.so, patched source files)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated code in liblzma that hooks into the sshd process, intercepts authentication routines, and enables remote code execution via specially crafted SSH keys or packets.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the OpenSSH server process (sshd), intercepts authentication routines, and enables a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by sending specially crafted authentication data, resulting in unauthorized remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces hidden hooks into a critical authentication process, which is not expected in a compression library. It enables remote code execution without user interaction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A compression library should only handle data compression/decompression, not interact with authentication or network processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; compression libraries should not interact with authentication or provide remote access.
key_indicators: Obfuscated and non-standard code in a widely used library
Enables remote code execution via non-standard input

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is introduced into the xz-utils/liblzma source code and distributed as part of official package releases (5.6.0, 5.6.1).
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of backdoored library on target systems

attack_chain.action: When the affected library is installed, it is loaded by system services such as OpenSSH (sshd) due to dynamic linking.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in memory and ready to intercept authentication routines

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends specially crafted SSH authentication data to the compromised system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in liblzma intercepts the data and triggers remote code execution

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized remote access and can execute arbitrary code on the system.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected hooks or code execution paths in liblzma or xz-utils libraries
Compression library code interacting with authentication or network processes
Obfuscated or non-standard code in open-source packages
file_indicators: liblzma.so with unexpected code sections or symbols
xz/liblzma source files with obfuscated or unfamiliar code
network_indicators: Unusual SSH authentication attempts with malformed or specially crafted keys
Unexpected outbound connections from sshd or compression library processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of xz-utils versions 5.6.0 or 5.6.1. Analyze liblzma.so for unexpected code or symbols. Audit SSH authentication logs for anomalous or malformed authentication attempts. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to system libraries. Employ behavioral analysis to detect compression libraries interacting with authentication or network processes.
